subject: 47 levels, the highest total this project has recorded. It is NOT a promotion, and the reason is the most useful part.

THE_CLOCK_a_correction_to_what_I_said_wh.what_I_intended: A short 2,700 s per-game mechanism screen on the quota remainder.
THE_CLOCK_a_correction_to_what_I_said_wh.what_the_log_shows: 'SCREEN: per-game clock 2700.0s, animation_retrieval=True'. The assignment DID take and DID print.
THE_CLOCK_a_correction_to_what_I_said_wh.what_actually_happened: Every game's final_wallclock_seconds is 7,920 s. The value was set on bm.solver and then overridden downstream, so this ran at FULL CLOCK.
THE_CLOCK_a_correction_to_what_I_said_wh.so: I asserted mid-run that the override 'did not take effect'. That was wrong: it took, and was overridden later. The effect I predicted (full clock) was right; the mechanism I gave for it was not.
THE_CLOCK_a_correction_to_what_I_said_wh.the_upside: Because it ran full clock it IS directly comparable to the GG2 controls, which the screen would not have been. It also cost 0.78 GPU-h more than the weekly cap; enforcement is at push time, so the run completed and the practical cost is nil.

RESULT.both_verdicts: TIE. |up-dn| = 5 against a measured null of 8.

THE_MECHANISM_BARELY_FIRED_AND_THAT_DECI.measured: Across 4 sampled games the model requested an animation ONCE, in ft09. ar25, lp85 and tr87: zero requests, while the harness flagged 4, 3 and 1 transitions respectively as worth_inspecting.
THE_MECHANISM_BARELY_FIRED_AND_THAT_DECI.control: 0 of 25 games, so retrieval is now non-zero and the prompt's promise is finally true.
THE_MECHANISM_BARELY_FIRED_AND_THAT_DECI.but: One request across four games cannot produce a 5-level gain. There is NO causal story connecting the treatment to the result.

THE_READING_THAT_MATTERS.what_GG7_actually_is: Its source dataset is BYTE-IDENTICAL to GG2's. The only difference is one boolean, and that boolean changed behaviour once in four games. So GG7 is, to a very good approximation, a byte-identical RERUN of GG2.
THE_READING_THAT_MATTERS.therefore: 47 against 44 and 40 is not evidence of improvement. It is a third sample of the SAME config, and it widens the measured run-to-run range of our shipped configuration to 40-47, mean 43.7.
THE_READING_THAT_MATTERS.and_that_is_worth_more_than_a_promotion: We now have three full-clock samples of one config instead of two. The within-config spread is 7 levels on this trio, which is consistent with the pooled sd of 8.21 and confirms that a single 47 means nothing on its own.

PREDECLARED_BAND_vs_DECISION.the_band_says: '>= 47: PROMOTE to a byte-identical replicate the same day, then the rotation.' 47 hits it exactly.
PREDECLARED_BAND_vs_DECISION.the_decision: NOT promoted to the rotation. The gate itself orders a replicate FIRST, and there is no quota for one until 2026-09-12. More importantly, the mechanism did not fire, so promoting would be promoting an UNEXPLAINED gain.
PREDECLARED_BAND_vs_DECISION.the_precedent_this_respects: Arm K went 44 then 28 on byte-identical bytes. Arm AE went 37 then 28 and its promotion was reverted the next day. Both reversals happened from exactly this position: one high run, no mechanism. Rule 15(b)'s cheap-promote arithmetic assumes a candidate has some prior of being BETTER; a config that is byte-identical apart from a boolean that fired once has no such prior.
PREDECLARED_BAND_vs_DECISION.what_DOES_change: GG7 still repairs a real defect: the prompt promised a function that did not exist, and the model demonstrably hunted for it. That repair is free and correct. It rides along with whatever ships next; it does not justify a rotation change by itself.

next: Replicate on 2026-09-12 as the gate orders. If a replicate also lands high with the mechanism still not firing, the honest conclusion is that our control estimate was too low, not that GG7 is better.
